_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); defense prime contractor signals

pit_profile.why: 'In 2018, 70% of our $53.8 billion in net sales were from the U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor (including 60% from the Department of Defense (DoD))' (FY2018 10-K, Item 1); 'We depend heavily on contracts with the U.S. Government for a substantial portion of our business. ... Those contracts are conditioned upon the continuing availability of Congressional appropriations.' (Item 1A): sales that depend on Congressional appropriations are not earnings that are the cycle, so DURABLE (the CAT and SO precedent); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) to public cloud displacing on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center outsourcing, ECOMMERCE (live from 2015-01-01) to e-commerce displacing physical retail, malls, grocery and distribution, STREAMING (live from 2015-08-04) to streaming displacing linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles, and ENERGY_TRANSITION (live from 2015-12-12) to decarbonisation stranding oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; the 10-K names no offshore competition, e-commerce or streaming and names cloud computing only among technological advances 'enabling new factors of competition for both traditional and non-traditional competitors', not as a substitute for its products; Lockheed Martin holds no oil, gas or coal reserves or refining, and the 10-K names oil and gas only as a market for Sikorsky's commercial helicopters ('demand for its products may be adversely affected by global economic conditions, including oil and gas trends that are outside of our control') and climate change only among concerns that could bring future regulation ('we could be affected by future regulations imposed or claims asserted in response to concerns over climate change, other aspects of the environment or natural resources'), so no disruption theme in scope is live

BEAR.desc: EPS -11.0%/yr (worst year FY09-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.1%/yr (FY19 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.1%/yr (FY09-FY18 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +20.7%/yr (best 2-yr run FY09-FY18); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: LMT (retrospective, 2019-08-30) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.59x (56.8% downside to Bear $166 / +35.6% upside to Bull $521) | Adj composite 2.51 vs market 2.85: gap -0.34 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +52% above the EPP floor $252 (12x FY19E $21.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: +12.8% total (+6.4%/yr) | At 18.3x FY19E the 15% hurdle price $508 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; backlog +30.2% in Q2 2019, forward revenues +8.3-11.1% (FY19 net sales guide); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) to public cloud displacing on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center outsourcing, ECOMMERCE (live from 2015-01-01) to e-commerce displacing physical retail, malls, grocery and distribution, STREAMING (live from 2015-08-04) to streaming displacing linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles, and ENERGY_TRANSITION (live from 2015-12-12) to decarbonisation stranding oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; the 10-Ks name no offshore competition, e-commerce or streaming and name cloud computing only among technological advances 'enabling new factors of competition for both traditional and non-traditional competitors', not as a substitute for its products; Lockheed Martin holds no oil, gas or coal reserves or refining, and the 10-Ks name oil and gas only as a market for Sikorsky's commercial helicopters ('demand for its products may be adversely affected by global economic conditions, including oil and gas trends that are outside of our control') and climate change only among concerns that could bring future regulation ('we could be affected by future regulations imposed or claims asserted in response to concerns over climate change, other aspects of the environment or natural resources'), so no theme in scope has dated evidence.
